locator: I q.44 a.1 ad 2, reply to the claim that what cannot not-be needs no efficient cause
interpretation: Aquinas rejects the necessity-therefore-uncaused inference, citing necessary principles causing necessary conclusions and Aristotle’s caused necessities. The demonstrative example is not by itself an efficient-cause ontology. The reply’s efficient-cause conclusion is retained without treating every necessary being as caused or proving every cause of esse is a cause of necessity. Reading is based on the verified complete Latin article and its objections/replies; no formal proof or independent premise truth is registered.
